nodes.procedure: Ti FP (thickness: 0.05 mm, size: 0.5 × 0.5 cm^2) was sonicated utilizing HCl solution (15 ml, 10 min) and then in water (15 ml, 5 min) and ethanol (15 ml, 5 min), followed by drying in air.

nodes.name: Electrochemical Hydrogenation Reconstruction
nodes.procedure: The electrochemical hydrogenation reconstruction was conducted using a standard three-electrode configuration H-type electrochemical cell containing Ti FP as the working electrode (WE), a platinum plate as the counter electrode (CE), and a Hg/HgO as the reference electrode (RE). The electrolyte was composed of 60 mmol KOH and 6 mmol KNO3 dissolved into 60 ml deionized water. The constant potential electrochemical hydrogenation reconstruction was then carried out at -1.3 V (vs. RHE) at 25 °C. The hydrogenation reconstruction time of titanium hydride was 3600 s. The electrode was thoroughly rinsed three times with deionized water. After hydrogenation reconstruction, the titanium hydride was carefully displaced from the electrolyte and rinsed three times with ethanol and water, then dried by Ar flow.

nodes.characterization_summary: The catalyst matches standard cubic TiH_{1.97} (PDF#07-0370) and hexagonal Ti (PDF#44-1294), confirming coexistence of Ti and TiH_{1.97} with no TiO2 or TiH2 peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern demonstrated that the catalyst matched well with the standard cubic TiH_{1.97} (PDF#07-0370) and hexagonal Ti (PDF#44-1294) (Fig. 1e), confirming that Ti and TiH_{1.97} coexist in the catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: Titanium hydride shows nanosheet morphology uniformly grown on titanium fiber.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images displayed that the obtained titanium hydride showed the nanosheet morphology and uniformly grew on titanium fiber (Fig. 1f, g and Supplementary Fig. S7).

nodes.characterization_summary: Titanium hydride nanosheets exhibit smooth surface consistent with SEM results.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, the titanium hydride nanosheets exhibited a smooth surface from the transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image (Fig. 1h), which was consistent with SEM results.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution HAADF-STEM shows d-spacings of 0.26 nm and 0.23 nm corresponding to (111) and (200) lattice planes of titanium hydride.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2a displays the high-resolution HAADF-STEM image of titanium hydride, where the marked d-spacings of 0.26 nm and 0.23 nm correspond to the (111) and (200) lattice planes of titanium hydride, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ti K-edge XAFS shows TiH_{1.97} has face-centered cubic structure with Ti-Ti bond length shifted to 2.72 Å from 2.52 Å in Ti foil.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ti K-edge XAFS spectra of TiH_{1.97}, the standard spectrum of Ti and TiH_2 were presented in Fig. 2d... the Ti foil exhibited a significant Ti-Ti scattering peak at 2.52 Å, which shifted to 2.72 Å in TiH_{1.97} in the Fourier transformed (FT-EXAFS)

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance C_dl = 18.47 mF cm^{-2} with NO3^- and 15.42 mF cm^{-2} without NO3^- (vs 0.45 and 0.61 mF cm^{-2} for Ti FP), indicating greater active sites on titanium hydride.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Titanium hydride exhibited a larger double-layer capacitance (C_dl) in NO3^- solution (18.47 mF cm^{-2}) than that in the solution without NO3^- (15.42 mF cm^{-2}), ... verifying the facilitated NO3^- coverage and adsorption.

nodes.characterization_summary: Nyquist plots show lower R_ct for titanium hydride than Ti FP in NO3^- electrolyte, corresponding to faster NIRR kinetics at electrode-electrolyte interface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The R_ct of titanium hydride was significantly lower than that of Ti FP in a 1 M KOH solution with 0.1 M NO3^-. The R_ct of titanium hydride in 1 M KOH solution with 0.1 M NO3^- was significantly smaller than in 1 M KOH

nodes.characterization_summary: Scraped black catalyst shows characteristic peaks at 35.0°, 40.6°, and 58.8° corresponding to (111), (200), and (220) lattice planes of TiH_{1.97}.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Besides, we scraped the black catalyst from the titanium fiber substrate and detected its phase structure through XRD. As shown in Supplementary Fig. S6, there are only three distinct characteristic peaks at 35.0°, 40.6°, and 58.8°, corresponding to the (111), (200) and (220) lattice planes of TiH_{1.97}.

nodes.characterization_summary: Selected area electron diffraction pattern shows well-crystallized titanium hydride.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern showed well-crystallized titanium hydride (Supplementary Fig. S8).
